test_title: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 14 Jun, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: A water tank can be filled in 38 minutes by using 44 pipes of the same capacity. In how many minutes (rounded off to two decimal places) will the water tank be filled if we use 37 pipes of the same capacity as above?
solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Total work = **Pipes × Time**

44 × 38 = 37 × Required Time

Required Time = (44 × 38) ÷ 37

Required Time = 1672 ÷ 37 ≈ 45.19

**∴ The correct answer is 45.19 minutes.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Number of initial pipes (M₁) = 44

Initial time taken (D₁) = 38 minutes

Number of final pipes (M₂) = 37

**Formula Used:**

M₁D₁ = M₂D₂

**Calculations:**

⇒ 44 × 38 = 37 × D₂

⇒ 1672 = 37 × D₂

⇒ D₂ = 1672 ÷ 37

⇒ D₂ = 45.1891...

⇒ D₂ ≈ 45.19 minutes

**∴ The correct answer is 45.19 minutes.**

**__Additional Information__**

Inverse Proportion

When the number of pipes increases, the time taken to fill the tank decreases, following the relation M₁T₁ = M₂T₂.

Pipes & Cisterns Efficiency

Total capacity is treated as constant work. Efficiency is directly proportional to the number of identical pipes used.</p
